turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My in-laws are visiting and I want the guest room to feel welcoming. Any ideas?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fresh sheets, an extra blanket and a couple of clean towels go a long way. A small lamp by the bed is nice too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I leave some snacks or water in there?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A bottle of water and a little basket of snacks is a lovely touch. Guests often feel shy raiding someone else's kitchen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about the wifi password, is it weird to / just leave a note?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not weird at all, it's really helpful. A small card on the nightstand works perfectly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Great. Maybe some flowers as well?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure, just pick something without a strong scent in case anyone has allergies.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm driving six hours to see my dad. How often should I stop?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A good rule is a short break every two hours. Stretch your legs, grab some water and rest your eyes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it better to leave really early in the morning?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Early is great for avoiding traffic, as long as you got a full night of sleep. Don't trade sleep for an early start.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was planning to leave at five / but maybe seven is smarter.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Seven sounds more reasonable. You'd still arrive by early afternoon with stops.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Any tips for staying alert on the highway?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Keep the car a little cool, listen to a podcast you enjoy and skip heavy meals. If you feel sleepy, pull over for a short nap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My grandparents are coming over and they don't really use phones. What can we do together?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Card games are usually a hit, or you could look through old photo albums and ask them for stories.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ooh, photo albums is a good one. My grandpa loves telling stories.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then that's perfect. You could even record a few of his stories to keep.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about food, they're kind of picky / and my grandma can't eat salt.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try a simple roast chicken with lemon and herbs instead of salt. Soft roasted vegetables on the side are usually safe too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And dessert?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A fruit crumble is easy and most grandparents love it. Serve it warm with a little cream.

option_sets.lead_in: My parents are visiting for the first time and I need help planning their big day out.
options: The first option is a boat tour around the harbor, about two hours, with lunch included.
Then there's the art museum, which my mom would love, but my dad might get bored.
And there's a big farmers market on Saturdays with live music and lots of local food.
moshi_comment: The boat tour is a nice compromise, since it's relaxing and lunch is sorted. The museum is perfect for your mom, but you'd need something for your dad afterward. The farmers market is easy and lively, but it can be tiring if they don't like crowds.
How do your parents feel about walking and crowds? If they're easygoing, I'd do the farmers market in the morning and the boat tour after. The museum could be a short stop on another day.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm visiting my brother next month and I have to choose how to get there.
options: One way is a direct flight, only an hour, but it leaves at six in the morning.
Another is the train, about five hours, cheaper, and I could work on my laptop.
Or I could drive, which takes four hours, but then I'd have the car while I'm there.
And the last option is the overnight bus, super cheap but probably not very comfortable.
moshi_comment: The train sounds like the best balance, since you can work and it's cheaper than flying. The flight is fastest, but that early start eats up most of the time you save. Driving only makes sense if you really need a car at your brother's place.
I'd skip the overnight bus unless money is really tight. Does your brother live somewhere you can get around without a car? If yes, take the train, and if not, driving might be worth it.
